findings.consequence: Comparing trajectories within the scope: batched trajectories have total step counts between 6 and 9, while non-batched trajectories have step counts between 11 and 14, confirming that tool call batching reduces total trajectory length and latency as stated in the hypothesis reason.
findings.spread: All trajectories fall within the single "all" batch and "all" stratum; both trajectories showing consecutive tool call batching and trajectories lacking it are distributed across the scope with no group confinement.
findings.statement: The assistant batches multiple tool calls consecutively in a single sequence before waiting for any tool results to return.

findings.consequence: The single trajectory with a failed tool call does exhibit immediate retry of the same tool with adjusted parameters, but no comparative cases exist to validate the pattern across the dataset.
findings.spread: No other trajectories fall within the scope of trajectories with at least one failed tool call.
findings.statement: Only one tool-use trajectory in the dataset contains a failed tool call, so there are fewer than two trajectories showing the behaviour, making confirmation impossible.

findings.consequence: Trajectories with intermediate messages between tool calls have total step counts of 11 and 14, while trajectories with zero intermediate messages have step counts of 9, matching the stated reason that intermediate messages increase trajectory length and latency without adding task value.

findings.statement: The number of short assistant acknowledgment messages inserted between tool calls and between the last tool call and the final synthesis varies between 0 and 3 across tool-use trajectories with three or more tool calls.
